nodes.title: Lifted CM types and critical coefficient indices
nodes.statement: Let L be totally imaginary of degree 2d and contain its maximal CM subfield K. A CM type Σ_K of K determines Σ={σ:L→ℂ | σ|K∈Σ_K}; its complement is denoted barΣ, without assuming a conjugation automorphism of L. Write I_L=ℤ[Hom(L,ℂ)]. A Hecke type μ is a norm pullback from K of μ₀ with μ₀(τ)+μ₀(barτ)=w independent of τ. For finite-index Γ⊂O_L×, HCI_L(Γ) consists of these types trivial on Γ. A type is critical for Σ when μ=β−α with α:Σ→ℕ strictly positive and β:barΣ→ℕ; equivalently μ=β−a−1 with a≥0. The negative embeddings must be exactly the lifted type. Prove that these are precisely the algebraic Hecke types whose Γ-invariant coefficient lines occur below. Fields with no CM subfield contribute no such critical type.
hypotheses: d≥1; specified embeddings into ℂ and a specified maximal CM subfield K when a critical type is present.
proofSteps: Import the infinity-type and unit-character classification from L0; restrict its admissibility condition along L/K.
Use the imported diagonalizable-group weight decomposition, then the unit theorem: a weight trivial on a finite-index subgroup is a Hecke type.
Separate the value exponent α from the derivative exponent a=α−1.
acceptance: A nonconstant assignment on embeddings above the same embedding of K is rejected even when its signs fit Σ.
No assertion that arbitrary totally imaginary fields are CM is used.

nodes.title: CM abelian data with bases and torsion
nodes.statement: A standard datum consists of a noetherian affine R⊂ℂ that is an O_(L^gal)[1/d_L]-algebra; an abelian scheme A/R of dimension d with O_L-action and Lie(A) of lifted type Σ; ordered bases ω_A=(ω_A,σ) of the rank-one cotangent eigensheaves and ω_A∨=(ω_A∨,barσ) of its dual's cotangent eigensheaves; and an f-torsion section x fixed by Γ. Bases are chosen after a localization or extension where the eigensheaves become free, not postulated for every base. The covariant H=(H¹_dR(A/R))∨ has H=H(barΣ)⊕H(Σ), H(barΣ)≃ω_A∨, and H(Σ)≃Lie A. The action on ω_A,σ is σ(γ)⁻¹, while that on ω_A∨,barσ is barσ(γ). The bases identify A(ℂ) with ℂ^Σ/Λ. For an ideal a the notation R[1/a] means the intersection of localizations away from primes dividing a, as in Notation 1.18; it does not silently invert every norm denominator.

Nf is a unit only for the unrefined torsion evaluation; KV.2/refined-evaluation has its own weaker assumption.

Trivialize the weight lines only after the permitted change of base and retain the isomorphisms under transport.

No construction of abelian schemes, generic Serre tensors or CM Hodge decompositions is repeated here.

nodes.title: Critical coefficient invariants
nodes.statement: For a,β≥0 put C_(a,β)=TSym^a(ω_A)⊗TSym^β(ω_A∨)⊗det(ω_A), with multigraded divided symmetric powers imported from P0. Its Γ-action has weight β−a−1. Over R contained in a number field, C_(a,β)^Γ=C_(a,β) when that weight belongs to CI_L(Γ), and is zero otherwise. More generally, for an R-torsion-free algebraic torus module M, its Γ-invariants are the direct sum of the weights trivial on Γ, identified with HCI_L(Γ) by the imported Hecke-type classification. The coefficient lines above are finite locally free, so they satisfy the torsion-free hypothesis. The generic weight decomposition itself exists in Tau Ceti for arbitrary modules; the extra hypothesis concerns invariants under the unit subgroup, not that decomposition.
hypotheses: Standard datum; finite-index Γ⊂O_L×; R embeds in a number field for the invariant-versus-zero assertion.
For the general assertion on M, require M to be R-torsion-free (finite locally free suffices). R being a domain alone does not imply this.
proofSteps: Compute weights using the Hodge decomposition and determinant.

Apply the native comodule weight decomposition and point-action formula. On a nontrivial unit weight choose γ with μ(γ)−1≠0; R-torsion-freeness forces its invariant vectors to vanish. This is the missing hypothesis in Proposition 1.5 (E14).
acceptance: At a=β=0 the determinant contributes −1 on each Σ embedding.
Do not replace Γ-invariants by invariants of a finite torsion subgroup or assert this dichotomy over arbitrary torsion coefficient rings.

For L=ℚ(ζ₃), R=ℤ[ζ₃,1/3], Γ=μ₆ and the weight 3σ, M=R/(2) has nonzero Γ-invariants although the weight is nontrivial over R: a primitive sixth root has weight −1, which becomes 1 modulo 2. The unrestricted-module version must be rejected.

nodes.title: Trace-zero functions on étale torsion
nodes.statement: For an isogeny δ:A→A′ such that δ and δ∨ are étale and commute with Γ, take D=ker δ or ker δ minus the identity section, provided Γ-stable. Let U=A\D and R[D]=H⁰(D,O_D); R[D]⁰=ker(Tr_(D/R)) and R[D]^(0,Γ) its Γ-invariants. Trace is the finite-étale algebra trace, so the construction makes sense before D splits into rational points. For c-regularization use D=A[c] and f_c=Nc·1_e−1_(A[c]). If x=e choose a second coprime c′ and D=A[cc′] minus e: under the Chinese-remainder identification extend by zero the pullback of f_c from (A[c′] minus e)×A[c]. This function has trace (Nc′−1)Tr(f_c)=0; restricting f_c itself to A[c] minus e would not have trace zero.
hypotheses: R affine; finite étale D/R; x∈U for every evaluation.
For D=A[c], Nc∈R× and c prime to the relevant torsion conductor; the two-auxiliary construction also requires Nc′∈R×.
proofSteps: Use the imported finite-étale algebra and trace and restrict the induced Γ-action.
Check the equality deg[c]=Nc by the CM ideal action, then compute the trace of f_c.
acceptance: Tr(f_c)=0 because A[c] has degree Nc, with no extra square on Nc.
D and x are disjoint in every downstream application.

nodes.title: Equivariant residue and inverse-limit comparison
nodes.statement: Put F_n=P^(n)⊗Ω_A^d and F=P_hat⊗Ω_A^d. The imported completed Poincaré trace gives H^i(A,Γ,F)=0 for i<d and H^d(A,Γ,F)≃R. For I the ideal of D, local complete-intersection duality gives Ext^q(I^k/I^(k+1),F_n)=0 for q<d and H^(q−d)(D,Hom(I^k/I^(k+1),i*P^(n))) for q≥d. Consequently support cohomology vanishes below d and contains R[D]^Γ canonically in degree d; its map to H^d(A,Γ,F) is Tr_(D/R). Prove H^(d−1)(U,Γ,F)≃lim_n H^(d−1)(U,Γ,F_n), including the vanishing inverse-limit obstruction used in Corollary 2.35. Do not infer vanishing of higher equivariant cohomology from the underlying coherent calculation.

Γ acts by automorphisms of A over the fixed base S; it acts trivially on S.
proofSteps: Import the top coherent Poincaré calculation and the equivariant spectral sequence.
Filter O_A/I^(k+1) by I^j/I^(j+1), use regular immersion duality and support localization.
Prove the required exactness/Milnor comparison for these particular pro-systems, using the SF.2 request rather than commuting cohomology and inverse limits formally.

The assertion is compatible with a nontrivial Γ-action on A over the fixed base S and is not H^i(A,F)^Γ by definition.

nodes.title: Equivariant coherent Eisenstein–Kronecker class
nodes.statement: Define EK_(Γ,A):R[D]^(0,Γ)→H^(d−1)(U,Γ,P_hat⊗Ω_A^d) as the unique preimage of the canonical degree-d support class of f under localization. This is an injective R-linear map with residue f and is compatible with its images at every finite Poincaré level. The definition uses derived equivariant sections in the category of Γ-linearized sheaves, not invariants taken after cohomology. Its naturality includes permitted flat base change, pullback through compatible isogeny/residue diagrams, and restriction of Γ.
hypotheses: Trace-zero datum and the residue calculation.
proofSteps: The trace of f is zero, so its support class lies in the localization kernel.
Vanishing below d makes the preimage unique; retain the full trace square to prove injectivity and naturality.
acceptance: Residue(EK(f))=f in the canonical supported submodule.
Flatness or an explicit base-change theorem accompanies each claimed scalar-extension compatibility.

Iterate the integrable Poincaré connection with its symmetric tensor convention, so that subsequent projection to a multi-index a produces the factorial a! in the analytic evaluation. The construction is made at finite levels and assembled as a compatible pro-class.

proofSteps: Apply the imported flat connection at each symmetric level and symmetrize by the P0 comparison convention.
Use integrability for the symmetric target and Γ-equivariance to descend to equivariant cohomology.
acceptance: The zero-th derivative is EK♮ itself.

nodes.title: Torsion specialization and group-cohomology moments
nodes.statement: Let x∈U(R) be fixed by Γ and killed by φ:A→B with φ∨ étale (equivalently the required lifted universal-extension map is étale). Pull ∇^a EK♮(f) back to x, apply the imported torsion splitting and the b-th moment, and use affine equivariant/coherent comparison. This defines Eis^(b,a)_Γ(f,x)∈H^(d−1)(Γ,TSym^a ω_A⊗TSym^b H⊗det ω_A). Here a,b are total nonnegative degrees; in multi-index notation a,β denote multi-indices with these total degrees. The splitting is the one normalized by the Poincaré rigidification, not an arbitrary trivialization at x.
hypotheses: Affine standard datum; x avoids D; φ∨ étale; f trace zero and Γ-invariant.
proofSteps: Evaluate the finite-level derivative on x, then take mom_b using P2/torsion-splitting and P2/group-moment-map.
Apply the SF.2 affine comparison to identify equivariant coherent cohomology on Spec R with group cohomology.
acceptance: The target contains H, not H¹_dR with the contravariant action.

nodes.title: Orientation-normalized critical Eisenstein classes
nodes.statement: First take Γ torsion-free of rank d−1. Project Eis^(b,a) through H→ω_A∨, then to the critical (a,β) component C_(a,β). Cap with the fundamental class of BΓ=Γ\EΓ, EΓ={(r_i)>0:∏r_i=1}, using the orientation ∧_(i<d)dr_i/r_i. An ordering of Σ also identifies det ω_A with the multidegree-one tensor line; the two permutation signs cancel. Use the rank-one divided-tensor identification u^[a]⊗u↦u^[a+1] on each weight line, rather than shuffle multiplication. This gives EK^(β,a)_Γ(f,x)∈TSym^(a+1)ω_A⊗TSym^βω_A∨. Its coordinate in the chosen divided-power bases is denoted e_(β,a). For Γ with finite torsion T, define the normalized version only after |T| is a unit: choose a free complement Γ₀, evaluate there, and divide by |T|. Prove independence of the complement after this localization. No integral map on arbitrary H^(d−1)(Γ,−) for all torsion Γ is asserted.

proofSteps: Use coefficient-invariants. The native logarithmic unit lattice and units-modulo-torsion equivalence identify Γ\EΓ with an oriented compact torus. Apply the requested comparison of group cohomology with its singular local-system model and the imported cap product. Glue the rank-one shift from local generators; its degree a+1 homogeneity makes it basis-independent.
Check ordering independence by simultaneous orientation and determinant changes.
Use transfer only in its valid form: in degree zero transfer across a finite-index subgroup multiplies by the index. The unrestricted surjectivity assertion in Proposition 2.27 is not used (E11).
acceptance: For d=1 and Γ=1 the cap product is ordinary degree-zero evaluation.
For Γ=μ₂ and Γ₀=1, normalized evaluation requires 1/2; it is not an arbitrary integral R-linear operation.

For critical β−α with α≥1, Γ(α+s)E^(β,α)(t′,s;Λ,Γ) equals d·Σ_(t∈T_Γ(t′))∫_(BΓ) Γ(|α|+ds)·K^(β+α)(H_r,t,0,|α|+ds,Λ)·∏_i(πr_i)^(α_i+s)/π^(|α|+ds) ·∧_(i<d)dr_i/r_i. Here Γ(α+s)=∏_iΓ(α_i+s). The leading d is the Jacobian of (r,u)↦(ur_i) on the product-one r-torus. Establish the equality in the convergence half-plane and its meromorphic continuation to the regular critical evaluation. The sum is over every torsion point in the orbit, not over one orbit representative.
hypotheses: Orbit-series hypotheses; convergence half-plane for initial unfolding; torsion-free Γ.
proofSteps: Unfold BΓ and the unit orbit simultaneously; use absolute convergence for Tonelli/Fubini initially.
Substitute positive coordinates to evaluate the product gamma integral.
Continue the identity meromorphically and evaluate at the regular critical point.
acceptance: The product gamma factor at s=0, α=a+1, equals a!.
For d=1 there is no r-integral and the identity reduces to the gamma factor times the lattice orbit sum.
The Jacobian factor is d: at d=2, dlog(ur₁)∧dlog(ur₂) has absolute coefficient 2 in dlog u∧dlog r₁.

nodes.title: Ordinary lifted types and CM level structures
nodes.statement: Fix a prime p∤d_L, p noninvertible on the arithmetic model, embeddings of algebraic numbers into ℂ and ℂ_p, and a lifted type Σ. It is p-ordinary when the sets of p-adic places induced by Σ and barΣ are disjoint and together cover all places over p; this definition applies to L containing K, without requiring L itself CM. Write O_L⊗ℤ_p=O_L(Σ_p)⊕O_L(barΣ_p). A Γ₀₀(p∞)-structure consists of O_L-equivariant compatible identifications μ_(p∞)⊗O_L(Σ_p)≃A[p∞]^connected and μ_(p∞)⊗O_L(barΣ_p)≃A∨[p∞]^connected. A Γ_arith-structure includes the compatible full connected and étale trivializations. Set p_Σ=∏_(v∈Σ_p)v and A_(n)=A(barp_Σ^n); q_n=[barp_Σ^n]:A_(n)→A is étale, with kernel A_(n)[barp_Σ^n], while its dual is connected. Via Weil pairings these data are equivalent to the specified trivializations of the complementary étale kernels. A prime-to-p ideal Betti structure induces them using the chosen compatible roots exp(2πi/p^n). In particular formal A≃Gm_hat⊗O_L(Σ_p), formal A∨≃Gm_hat⊗O_L(barΣ_p), with character modules the corresponding dual Tate modules. The paired isogeny [p_Σ^n]:A→A_(n) composes with q_n to [p^n].

nodes.title: The p-adic theta function of a residue class
nodes.statement: For a torsion section y∈U killed by an isogeny with étale dual, restrict EK_Γ(f) to the formal neighborhood of y, translate to the identity, and use the imported ordinary Poincaré trivialization on formal A×formal A∨. Cap the resulting degree-(d−1) group-cohomology class with the same torsion-free oriented fundamental cycle and identify det ω_A using ω_can(A). This defines θ_Γ(f,y)∈H⁰(formal A×formal A∨,O). It is integral over O_(ℂ_p). For arbitrary torsion y the same procedure gives a generic-fiber theta function; integrality then requires an extra argument. Restriction to a finite-index torsion-free subgroup scales theta by the subgroup index.
hypotheses: Torsion-free Γ fixes y and f; ordinary level structures; f trace zero.
Integral version requires the killing dual étale; torsion-normalized Γ requires its order invertible or the G3 divisibility input.
proofSteps: Apply the P4 translation and infinitesimal trivializations and their compatibility with the rigidification.
Use Lemma 5.15 to cap formal functions with the canonical determinant differential.
Check integral and generic constructions agree under the injective base change.
acceptance: Do not declare every summand in the translation formula integral.

This target specializes that formula to the CM bases and the Hodge moment maps; it does not re-own multivariate Amice theory.

nodes.title: The CM Eisenstein measure and its moments
nodes.statement: Let μ_Eis,Γ(f,x) be the bounded O_(ℂ_p)-valued measure on the additive finite free ℤ_p-module O_L⊗ℤ_p corresponding to θ_Γ(f,x) under the basis-independent multivariate Amice isomorphism. Use Mathlib AbstractMeasure for the underlying continuous linear functional. For critical β−a−1 its moments satisfy (Ω_p^(a+1)(Ω_p∨)^β)⁻¹∫t^a s^β dμ_Eis=e_(β,a), the coordinate of EK in the algebraic divided-power bases. More generally the projected noncritical coefficient components vanish under the corresponding Γ-weight condition. Dependence on f is linear and subgroup normalization follows that of theta.
hypotheses: Integral theta data; coefficient ring O_(ℂ_p); finite free rank 2d module.
The multivariate, coefficient-complete, equivariant Amice contract in the L2 request is needed; a one-variable field statement alone is insufficient.

Compare invariant derivatives, Poincaré moments and the canonical cap with EK.
Rescale ω_A and ω_A∨ by their p-adic periods; the exponent on Ω_p is a+1.
acceptance: At a=β=0 the total mass is Ω_p^1 times the (0,0) EK coordinate, not just that coordinate.
Transport under an integral basis change of O_L⊗ℤ_p gives the same measure.

nodes.title: p-power translation with Weil-pairing weights
nodes.statement: Let q_n:A_(n)=A(barp_Σ^n)→A be as in ordinary-level; pull back D and f to D′ and f′. For Γ-invariant s∈A[p_Σ^n], t∈A∨[barp_Σ^n], let s′ be the unique p_Σ^n-torsion lift of s and x′ the unique f-torsion lift of x. Then (T_s×T_t)*θ_(Γ,A)(f,x)=Σ_(u∈ker q_n)⟨u,t⟩_(q_n)·q_(n),# θ_(Γ,A_(n))(f′,x′+s′+u). The equality is interpreted through the formal isogeny identifications in the generic fiber. Its left side is integral; individual right-hand theta functions need not be integral because q_n∨ is not étale.
hypotheses: Ordinary theta data, p∤f, Γ fixes the torsion translations.
proofSteps: Compare the supported residue functions under the Poincaré isogeny and translation diagrams.
Identify the multiplier by the rigidified Weil pairing, with the same order of its arguments.
Use uniqueness of the localized EK class and the compatibility of formal cap and trivialization.
acceptance: The Weil pairing occurs with the positive power here; the inverse is in the Fourier transform below.
Integrality of the sum is deduced from the left side, never termwise.

nodes.title: Normalized partial Fourier transform
nodes.statement: At level p^n let x∈A_(n)∨[p_Σ^n], y∈A_(n)[p_Σ^n], and z∈A_(n)[barp_Σ^n]. With q_n=[barp_Σ^n]:A_(n)→A, the perfect pairing for [p_Σ^n]:A→A_(n) pairs q_n(y) with x. For a function ρ on the two étale coordinate modules define P_Aρ(y,z)=p^(−dn)Σ_x⟨q_n(y),x⟩_[p_Σ^n]⁻¹ρ(x,z). Fourier transformation acts only in the Σ-direction; the other variable is retained. The generic-fiber denominator p^(dn) is mandatory. Under the complex ideal uniformization this becomes the normalized finite trace-exponential sum exp(−2πi Tr_(L/ℚ)(xy)) in equation (5.5.11), with the ideal-coordinate denominators specified there.
hypotheses: Chosen compatible Γ₀₀-levels and primitive p^n-th roots; functions at a finite level; generic coefficient field containing the roots.
proofSteps: Define the transform from the perfect pairing and the actual finite group of order p^(dn).
Prove inversion and orthogonality by finite character sums, then compare the trace-pairing coordinates.
acceptance: The denominator is the order of one direction, not p^(2dn).
Fourier coefficients can have p-denominators even when ρ is integral.

nodes.title: Katz’s local factor for a lifted ordinary type
nodes.statement: Let χ have infinity type β−α and conductor dividing p∞f. Define χ_fin on (O_L⊗ℤ_p)× by χ((λ))=χ_fin(λ)·λ^(β−α) for λ prime to pf and congruent to 1 modulo f, with μ evaluated at the embedding σ in the exponent (correction E5). Put Ftilde(x,y)=χ_fin(x⁻¹,y). For each v|p extend its v-component to O_(L,v) by the constant function 1 when v∈Σ_p and that unit-character component is trivial, and by zero off the units otherwise. Let F be the product. Choose ∏_(v∈Σ_p)v^(a_v)=(c)b with c≡1 mod f and b prime to p. Then Local(χ,Σ)=c^(α−β)·(PF)(c⁻¹)/χ(b), where c^(α−β) means (N_(L/K)c)^α₀/(overline(N_(L/K)c))^β₀ in the chosen embedding indices. Prove this scalar is nonzero, independent of the conductor decomposition, and compatible with the L0 Gauss-sum convention. Distinguish F from the zero extension of Ftilde; their difference at an unramified Σ-place produces an Euler factor.
hypotheses: Ordinary lifted type; embeddings and additive trace character fixed; PF is exactly KV.7/partial-fourier.
χ_fin uses the ideal-character convention of partial-l-identity, not its inverse.
proofSteps: Choose c by approximation in the required ray congruence class.
Factor the finite Fourier transform locally; use primitive-character Gauss-sum nonvanishing and the constant-function orthogonality at trivial Σ-components.
Change c by a principal ray element and check the monomial, finite-character and ideal factors cancel.
acceptance: For all p-local components unramified take c=b=1; the local factor is 1.
Replacing the constant extension by zero extension at a trivial Σ-place changes the expression and is rejected.

In conductor one also define δ′_(c′)=δ_1−δ_(Art(c′)), with value 1−χ(c′). The products of these atoms with a measure mean convolution in the imported Iwasawa/measure algebra. In particular δ_c is different from the scalar factor χ(c)Nc−1 in the complex integrality theorem; they differ by the unit χ(c).
hypotheses: c prime to pf; c′ prime to pc when used; norm embedded into the coefficient ring.
proofSteps: Use Mathlib Dirac measures, addition and scalar multiplication; import convolution rather than define a private group algebra.
Evaluate a Dirac measure at χ, then apply χ(c⁻¹)=χ(c)⁻¹.
acceptance: The Artin inverse belongs in the support of δ_c.

nodes.title: Smoothed ray-class measures from the CM Eisenstein measure
nodes.statement: For f≠O_L construct bounded measures μ_(f,c) by choosing ray-class representatives a_i, the Serre tensors A_i=(a_i⁻¹f)⊗A and their compatible periods, evaluating μ_Eis at x_i=Ω mod a_i⁻¹fΩ, and restricting to (O_L⊗ℤ_p)×. Set U_f=O_f× (global units congruent to 1 mod f), G⁰_f=(O_L⊗ℤ_p)×/closure(U_f), and use the exact sequence 1→G⁰_f→G_f→Cl_f→1. On each coset push the weighted measure by (t,s)↦q_f(t⁻¹,s), with weight ∏_(σ∈Σ)σ(t)⁻¹, then sum the finitely many cosets. This uses U_f, not all global units for nontrivial tame f (E12). Under the completed sign normalization G1 and unit-index normalization G3, its moments are δ_c(χ) times the right side of the final interpolation formula. For f=O_L use two coprime auxiliaries and the function pulled back from f_c on (A[c′]\{e})×A[c], yielding μ_(O_L,c,c′) with the extra factor δ′_(c′)(χ).
hypotheses: Ordinary based datum, tame f prime to p, compatible ideal structures and roots of unity.
Unit subgroup changes used to fix finite levels carry their exact index; normalized integral descent requires G3.
proofSteps: Use the native abstract-measure pushforward and the imported L2 continuous weighting/projection formula. Restrict to the clopen unit locus by extension of test functions by zero, then apply the indicated continuous inversion and determinant weight; compactness makes these operations bounded.
Show the correct tame-unit quotient and representatives identify it with the ray-class tower.
Insert the locally constant moment formula; compute ramified local factors from PF and unramified corrections from the difference between F and the zero extension.
Use the corrected explicit EK formula and complete G1 before identifying its moment sign with the unsigned target.

nodes.title: Bounded removal of auxiliary ideals
nodes.statement: Establish a bounded O_(ℂ_p)-valued measure μ_f independent of c such that δ_c*μ_f=μ_(f,c) when f≠O_L, and δ_c*δ′_(c′)*μ_(O_L)=μ_(O_L,c,c′) when f=O_L. The required output is a continuous O_(ℂ_p)-linear functional on C(G_f,O_(ℂ_p)) with norm at most one. Prove it by an integral measure-algebra divisibility argument or by Kummer congruences: every finite linear combination of admissible character twists that takes values in p^m O_(ℂ_p) must have the corresponding combination of proposed moments in p^m O_(ℂ_p), uniformly in the finite quotient and m. Treat torsion components of G_f, shared zeros of the smoothing factors and conductor one explicitly. Merely knowing that each individual character value is integral, or that the family has greatest common divisor one in an unspecified ring, does not prove this statement. This source-to-boundedness step is gap G2.

All density arguments are made for continuous linear functionals with an established bound.

Prove the uniform congruences/divisibility before extending the candidate functional by continuity.
Show the auxiliary relations identify all resulting bounded extensions, including across the conductor-one cancellation.

For a p-ordinary lifted type Σ of L and a tame integral ideal f prime to p, construct a bounded O_(ℂ_p)-valued measure μ_f on G_f=Gal(L(p∞f)/L) such that for every critical algebraic χ of conductor dividing p∞f and infinity type β−α,
(Ω_p^α(Ω_p∨)^β)⁻¹∫_(G_f)χ(g)dμ_f(g)=𝒩_(α,β)(Local(χ,Σ)·∏_(v∈Σ_p)(1−χ(v⁻¹)/Nv)·∏_(v∈barΣ_p)(1−χ(v))·L_f(χ,0)).
At a prime ramified in χ set the corresponding ideal-character value to zero so the omitted Euler factor is one; χ(v⁻¹)=0 in that convention is not the inverse of zero. Primitive versus f-imprimitive L-functions are related by exactly the displayed depletion factors. Prove uniqueness from the finite-order-twist density after boundedness has been established. This is the target of Theorem 5.27 with the explicit G1–G3 proof obligations, not a claim that they have been discharged. At L=K, tame conductor f=O_K and the overlapping Katz infinity types −kΣ−Σ_σ d(σ)(σ−barσ), k≥1 and d(σ)≥0, compare with the existing L3 Katz measure under the same periods, Artin convention, local factors and primitive/imprimitive convention. The current L3 target does not supply a comparison for arbitrary tame f or every critical type.
hypotheses: Ordinary standard datum, O_L Betti structure, complex and p-adic periods fixed; all characters read through the chosen embeddings.
G1 sign comparison, G2 bounded desmoothing and G3 integral unit normalization must be proved.
proofSteps: Combine the corrected smoothed interpolation with bounded-desmoothing.
At ramified and unramified Σ-places compute the separate Fourier contributions; collect the complete barΣ-depletion.
Use density for uniqueness after boundedness. Compare with L3/katz-padic-l-function only at L=K, f=O_K and its stated overlapping infinity-type range, after transporting the conventions.
acceptance: Test d=1 with a split ordinary prime, d>1 with L=K, and a non-CM quartic containing K.
An inert prime for an imaginary quadratic K is outside this theorem; it belongs to the independent nonordinary direction.
Period rescaling agrees with the algebraic differential scaling on both sides.
The general interpolation target allows tame f prime to p and arbitrary admissible critical β−α; only its Katz comparison is restricted to the existing supplier’s smaller range.

requests.need: Supply the inverse-limit comparison for the actual finite-level equivariant coherent complexes of the completed Poincaré sheaf (including the required R¹lim vanishing), affine torsion evaluation into group cohomology, and a Borel smooth/coherent comparison for a discrete unit group. Use the existing equivariant-derived-functor and localization nodes; do not infer these comparisons from the spectral-sequence name alone.

Extend the imported Dolbeault comparison by LF topology on compactly supported test forms and the local regularization/Poincaré lemma proving a bundle-valued current resolution on the noncompact CM Borel manifold, compatible with the finite-level Poincaré connection. Generic manifolds/forms already belong to current DifferentialGeometry.

Supply integration of the top real unit-torus form, Stokes for the specified current model, and compatibility of analytic residue/trace with the algebraic coherent trace. Generic integration and de Rham theory remain with current DifferentialGeometry.

Supply the ordinary connected–étale decomposition and perfect Cartier/Weil pairings for finite-flat p-power torsion with O_L-idempotents; prove compatibility of the two paired isogenies and levels. This roadmap only specializes them to the lifted CM type.

Supply a basis-independent Amice equivalence between bounded O_(ℂ_p)-valued measures on the finite-free rank-2d ℤ_p-module O_L⊗ℤ_p and integral functions on its formal character torus. Include product/base-change naturality, translations and invariant differential moments, so changing the two CM bases commutes with the transform; the one-variable field-valued range theorem alone does not supply this integral interface.

Supply localization of the commutative integral measure/Iwasawa algebra on a ray-class profinite abelian group and a criterion for a compatible fraction to be a bounded integral measure, stated by uniform Kummer congruences or integral divisibility. Include torsion components and common zeros of auxiliary atoms; a characterwise integrality assertion is insufficient.

Supply the rank-one Hecke motive M(χ), its comparison/period line and restriction-of-scalars/tensor and norm-pullback compatibilities in the convention χ of type β−α. Supply algebraic period factors for finite-order twists and Tate twists. Kings–Sprang §4.5 invokes Deligne Propositions 8.18 and 8.21; these are inputs, not assertions that those original pages were read here.

Supply Deligne criticality for the same Hecke-motive normalization, and the CM period expression for c⁺ modulo Qbar×. Keep the period relation (nonzero periods modulo Qbar×) separate from the normalized L-value, which can vanish.

Make the admissible Weil type set Ξ explicit: types trivial on some finite-index unit subgroup are norm pullbacks from the maximal CM subfield with parallel conjugate sum; when there is no CM subfield they are parallel norm powers. Identify Ξ with that classification, not just a necessary parallel-weight condition. Kings–Sprang §1.1, pp.7–8 supplies the needed interface; the original Serre source is not claimed as read here.

Use Stage 5 items 3–4 for finite-cover transfer and the exterior-power homology of a product of circles. Supply the comparison between native discrete group (co)homology for a finite-rank free abelian Γ and singular (co)homology of Γ\EΓ through its contractible logarithmic universal cover, compatible with finite-index maps and the coefficient representation. The existing finite-deck Cartan–Leray theorem alone is not a comparison for the infinite deck group Γ. Dirichlet’s logarithmic lattice is already in Mathlib.

Supply the singular local-coefficient cap product and fundamental class for the oriented compact connected real torus Γ\EΓ, with Γ torsion-free, and naturality under its finite covers. Use the existing orientation and Stage 5 comparison; identify the cap in top degree with the coefficient line and prove its projection formula. No surjective integral transfer through finite torsion is assumed.

gaps.title: Residue, current and p-adic sign comparison
gaps.detail: Prove the single commuting comparison from the algebraic residue normalization through the corrected current and the oriented unit fundamental cycle to the invariant p-adic differential. Local exterior-algebra checks force the recurrence and the factor (−1)^(|β|+1), but do not alone determine its cancellation or transport in the final unsigned interpolation convention. Track every determinant permutation, conjugate-dual identification and t↦t⁻¹ coordinate change; do not assume Theorem 5.27’s proof Step 1 resolves it.

gaps.title: Uniform bounded division of smoothing factors
gaps.detail: Prove the integral Iwasawa-algebra divisibility or uniform Kummer congruences in KV.8/bounded-desmoothing. The finite C_p example gives an explicit obstruction to deriving boundedness merely from integral individual character values. The cited de Shalit auxiliary-ideal argument was not accessible in a cleared source; no theorem from it is claimed as read.

gaps.title: Integral descent to full unit groups
gaps.detail: The torsion-free cap is integral; normalized full-unit cap can require division by the torsion order. Prove the required specific divisibility for the trace-zero residue classes at all nonunit unit-group indices. Proposition 2.27’s unrestricted homology-transfer argument does not provide it. This affects the integral critical-value theorem and the bounded p-adic construction, without asserting that either published theorem is false.

design.brief:
First prerequisite: Ray-class distributions and general automorphic constructions (AutomorphicPadicLFunctions). Import its Hecke-character/period interfaces but not an ordinary-CM hypothesis at an inert prime. Complex multiplication and explicit reciprocity (ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity CM.4) owns the canonical Hecke character and Gross Q-curve realization; Global number fields (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GlobalNumberFields) and Class field theory (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory) own Hecke carriers and ray-class fields. Import Bloch–Kato maps from p-adic Hodge regulators (PadicHodgeRegulators L1) and continuous tower cohomology from SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0/L3.

This roadmap is independent of Rubin's decomposition. It proves the canonical root number +1 for the auxiliary K with 2 split, existence of l satisfying (3.3), period normalization, integral elliptic-unit zeta classes, Kato Proposition 15.9 in BKO's conjugated-character/dual/Tate convention, disjointness and local splitting for the ξ_ν projection, and the root-number parity formula for nontrivial χ. Prove Finis Theorem 1.1(2)'s specialization (3.9), with the prime-name switch explicit: Finis's tower p is BKO's split l, while Finis's valuation ℓ is BKO's inert p. Verify μ and b vanish using canonical conductor and good reduction, compare the critical-point/infinity-type conventions, and prove the removed l-factor equals 1 (the conductor of φ̄ν is f·l^m). The result is Ω^(-1)L_f(barφν,1)∈W× for all but finitely many ν. Do not use Hsieh's ordinary μ theorem in its place.

There must be ONE general elliptic-unit foundation. PAPER-BURUNGALE-TIAN-26's accepted route 7 proposes CMAllPrimeMainConjectures for it (design pending): import its elliptic-unit layer and never duplicate it privately. This route owns BKO's normalized analytic applications that feed the local optimal-unit proof of AnticyclotomicLocalUnits. Rubin's p-adic L-function, which imports that local decomposition, is planned in InertAnticyclotomicCMMainConjecture (route 5), so the graph NonordinaryCMSpecialValues → AnticyclotomicLocalUnits → InertAnticyclotomicCMMainConjecture is acyclic (FIX-RT-PAPER-BURUNGALE-KOBAYASHI-OTA-21). Each definition gets API, three tests and eventual suggested Lean signatures; include conjugation, inverse-character and Euler-factor regression tests. Import from Finite flat group schemes and integral p-adic Hodge theory, Part II: Lubin–Tate formal modules and quasi-canonical lifts (LubinTateFormalModulesAndQuasiCanonicalLifts) the Lubin–Tate group F and the identification of an elliptic lift with a_(p²) = −2p with F (lt-lift-identification); rubin-cm-lubin-tate applies it to the CM curve (FIX-RT-PAPER-BURUNGALE-KOBAYASHI-OTA-21). Hecke carriers are Global number fields (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GlobalNumberFields) Layer 9; Hecke L-functions, their functional equation and root numbers are Automorphic L-functions and local factors (AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.1), for canonical-sign and twisted-root-sign.
